```{=html}
{{< include assets/diagrams/tool-landscape.svg >}}
```

::: notes
- Read it with the architecture slide in mind: the further right, the closer the work
  runs to the data.
- Browser: Plotly, Altair / Vega-Lite, deck.gl (+ pydeck) and lonboard (deck.gl with
  GeoArrow in Jupyter). The data travels to the browser; WebGL helps, but the browser's
  memory is the limit.
- Python server or kernel: HoloViz (Datashader, HoloViews, hvPlot, Panel) and Dask:
  today's demo.
- Query engines: DuckDB, Polars (its GPU engine, still open beta, runs on cuDF), Mosaic,
  VegaFusion.
- GPU: RAPIDS cuDF (also cudf.pandas: pandas on the GPU without code changes).
  Datashader itself runs on CPU, Dask or GPU.
- Versions checked September 2026: plotly.py 7.1, Altair 6.3 / Vega-Lite 6.4, deck.gl
  9.4, lonboard 0.16, Datashader 0.19, HoloViews 1.23, hvPlot 0.12, Panel 1.9, Dask
  2026.8, DuckDB 1.5, Polars 1.44, Mosaic 0.31, VegaFusion 2.0, cuDF 26.08.
- Left off on purpose: plotly-resampler (maintenance mode; successor FlexViz) and
  cuxfilter (sunset by RAPIDS, archived July 2026).
- Which datashader glyphs work on which containers (pandas, Dask, cuDF, SpatialPandas,
  xarray): datashader.org/user_guide/Performance.html#data-objects
:::

::: source
[holoviz.org](https://holoviz.org)
:::

::: notes
- HoloViz: eight libraries that work together (the site lists exactly these, checked
  September 2026).
- hvPlot: one-line interactive plots from pandas, xarray, Dask and more.
- Datashader: rasterizes huge data on the server into images or aggregates.
- HoloViews: annotate the data with what it means and the plot follows; with
  datashade / rasterize it makes datashader interactive (the census maps).
- Lumen: data-driven dashboards from YAML specs (recent versions add LLM-assisted
  exploration).
- Panel: the app layer (the live cells run on it); Param: declarative parameters;
  Colorcet: perceptually uniform colormaps (fire); GeoViews: geographic HoloViews.
:::
